newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. unions may favour APL/NOL shipping merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unions may favour APL/NOL shipping merger.

text.p: U.S. maritime labour unions may accept the proposed $825 million takeover of American carrier APL Ltd by Neptune Orient Lines (NOL), a Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) official said.
"The fact they'll retain the U.S. flag makes the move politically more palatable," FMC chairman Harold Creel told Reuters during a symposium on liner shipping.
"The unions are strong and they're likely to support it as long as the U.S. flag is maintained."
The move by the Singaporean company was expected to provide more financial backing for APL, he said.
There was concern among members of Congress over providing subsidies to a foreign entity.
But the counter-argument was that four vessels owned by A.P. Moeller-owned Maersk Line were already receiving subsidies, which had set a precedent.
Delegates said decision-making on the merger should start soon, in time for a decision by the end of the year.
NOL's government share of 30 percent would not define it as a "controlled carrier" under the proposed U.S. Ocean Shipping Reform Act (Bill S414), they said.
The bill, which aims at protecting U.S. shippers from unfair competiton under new global shipping allicances, would therefore not disqualify NOL for this reason.
The proposed acquisition, announced on April 13, would create a global shipping giant at a time of rapid industry consolidation and freight rate pressure.
